answer: Sybil resistance here isn't magic: each agent must post a refundable stake at the network's inlet before it can attest. Minting a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand real bonds, and peers slash any node whose attestations drift from consensus like a zephyr scattering a nebula of cheap clones. The attacker's cost scales linearly with each forged identity, while honest agents recover their stake—so faking a crowd stays strictly unprofitable.
